one_month_reasoning: The Q3 2026 date is still unconfirmed by Reddit as of 2026-10-05: there is no 8-K or release. MarketBeat estimates Thu 29 Oct and says it is unconfirmed. TipRanks/Investing list Wed 4 Nov after the close, which would put the reaction outside the window (the window ends at the 4 Nov close). Reddit's last four reports were month-end Thursdays, so I put about 57% on the gap landing inside the window. Q3 guide is $860-870M (+47-49%) with adj. EBITDA $385-395M. Reddit beat the top of guidance by ~10-11% in Q1 and Q2, but Q2 still fell ~12-21% because US DAUq was flat QoQ. This is the first quarter without the logged-in/logged-out split. September traffic is seasonally weak: DA Davidson cut its PT to $185 on that (17 Sep), and Similarweb shows visits -3.2% m/m. Both sides have fuel. Short interest is ~14% of float, a squeeze risk on a clean print, and users and traffic are the downside. I take no directional view. The model is a mixture: 57% event-month with a 21.5% monthly sigma, 43% quiet month with 15.5% (ex-earnings vol). The median is ~$150.9 (slightly below spot from volatility drag), so P(>= spot) = 0.49.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods on Oct-2027 NTM numbers (0.25 x CY27 + 0.75 x CY28), each with a normal 22% tax and 207M diluted shares: 35% P/E 17.6x (11-peer median) on taxed adjusted EPS $9.65 = $170; 35% P/E 22x (median of the SBC-expensed peers META/GOOGL/NFLX/SPOT) on taxed GAAP EPS $6.86 = $151; 30% SBC-burdened, tax-normalized FCF $1.41B at a 4.75% yield + $3.5B net cash = $160. Blend = $160.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM (Oct-2027) taxed adjusted EPS $9.65 = 0.25 x CY27 $8.12 + 0.75 x CY28 $10.16, x 17.6x (consistent-basis 11-peer median)

inputs_detail.input: CY2027 adjusted EPS consensus (SBC added back, nearly untaxed)

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2'26 tax was ~$4M on ~$257M pretax because of the full US valuation allowance. The 10-Q says a significant release is reasonably possible within 12 months, after which book tax normalizes to roughly 21% federal plus state. CY27 taxed adjusted EPS = 9.69 - 0.22 x 7.14 (GAAP pretax/share) = $8.12.

Growth keeps decelerating, from 61% (Q2'26) to a 48% Q3 guide to 32% consensus for CY27, and I extend the path to ~21%. Skeptic-leaning but in line with the deceleration path; no extra EPS haircut is applied (round 1's 10% haircut is removed per supervisor).

inputs_detail.input: CY2028 adj. EBITDA margin / SBC / other
inputs_detail.derivation: Q3 guide implies ~45% adj. EBITDA margin and CY27 consensus ~46%. SBC of ~12% of revenue is implied by the CY27 gap between adjusted $9.69 and GAAP $7.07 (x 207M = $0.54B on $4.46B) and trends down slightly. Interest is ~3.5% on ~$3.5B cash. GAAP pretax = $1.94B, or $9.35/share. Taxed adjusted EPS = $10.16.

Median of 11 peers on StockAnalysis CY2027 consensus EPS (one calendar-year basis, all December FYs, SPOT converted from EUR). No premium: Reddit's faster growth (CY27 rev +32% vs ~13% peer median) is offset by Google traffic dependence and a licensing renewal, both structural through the horizon (10-Q). See comps_summary for the SBC caveat on this basis.
Fully diluted 207.0M at 30 Jun 2026; buybacks (~$235M/qtr) roughly offset SBC dilution.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM taxed GAAP EPS $6.86 = 0.25 x CY27 $5.57 + 0.75 x CY28 $7.29, x 22x (median of the peers whose consensus EPS already expenses SBC)

inputs_detail.derivation: $7.07 consensus includes ~1% tax, so pretax is ~$7.14; at 22% tax that is $5.57. (The supervisor's ~$5.9 implies ~17% tax; I use 22% consistently.)
GAAP pretax $1.94B (see method 1 CY28 build) x 0.78 / 207M.

META 21.3x, GOOGL 23.0x, NFLX 17.6x and SPOT 26.7x are the peers whose consensus EPS bears SBC; their median is 22.2x. I use 22x, at that median. Reddit's growth is higher, but its third-party traffic dependence is higher too, so neither a premium nor a discount is proven persistent.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM revenue $5.17B x 46.5% adj. EBITDA = $2.40B, less capex $0.03B, SBC $0.57B and normalized 22% tax = FCF $1.41B; / 4.75% = $29.6B + $3.5B net cash = $33.1B / 207M

inputs_detail.derivation: 0.25 x $4.46B CY27 consensus + 0.75 x $5.40B CY28 estimate.
Fixes round 1, which ignored SBC: SBC is a real cost to owners, and the buyback only offsets it.
NOLs keep cash tax low for a while. I treat that as a temporary benefit and do not capitalize it as perpetual, which is conservative by a few dollars/share.

The inverse of the ~22x GAAP-peer P/E is ~4.5%. I add ~0.25pt because FCF here excludes interest income while net cash is added separately, and for a shorter public track record. This is one risk adjustment only (no EPS haircut).
$2.786B at 30 Jun 2026 with no debt, plus ~$1.1-1.3B FCF over 5 quarters, less buybacks of ~$235M/qtr ($760M authorization left).

bear.story: Google AI Overviews and AI answer engines keep eroding logged-out traffic and US DAUq declines for several quarters. The Google licence renewal goes badly (only $30.1M of licensing RPO is contracted for 2027). CY27 revenue growth slows to ~20%, and CY28 GAAP taxed EPS lands near $5.5, which at ~18x is ~$100. That is the low end of the GAAP-peer range and consistent with the ~$100 technical target bears cite.

base.story: Orderly deceleration: 61% to ~32% in CY27 and ~21% in CY28, with stable US users and adj. EBITDA in the mid-40s%. The stock trades at peer-median multiples on taxed NTM earnings (17.6x adjusted / 22x GAAP), which is my fair value.

bull.story: International growth and ad pricing keep CY27 growth at 38%+ and CY28 at ~28%, and the licence is renewed at higher value. Taxed adjusted NTM EPS is ~$11.2, or ~$8.2 taxed GAAP, and the multiple moves to ~20x adjusted / ~27x GAAP, the upper part of the peer range. That gives ~$225.

comps_summary.peer_range: CY2027 consensus P/E 7.3x (SNAP) to 38.7x (ROKU) across 11 peers, all on StockAnalysis CY2027 consensus EPS (December fiscal years, so one calendar-year basis; SPOT EUR EPS converted at ~1.17). Interquartile range is ~8.9x-23.0x. Forward EV/EBITDA could not be sourced consistently (vendor pages are paywalled), so it is not used.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: RDDT is 15.7x CY27 adjusted EPS untaxed and 18.7x once taxed at 22% ($151.69/$8.12), and 27.2x on taxed GAAP EPS ($5.57). I use the 17.6x median on taxed adjusted EPS and 22x, the median of the SBC-expensed sub-group, on taxed GAAP EPS. Both are at the median, inside the range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium or discount. Reddit's faster growth is real (CY27 revenue +32% vs a peer median of ~13%), but I cannot show it persisting through Oct-2027 against structural, filing-documented offsets: the 10-Q search-engine dependence risk factor, US DAUq flat QoQ, the end of logged-in/out disclosure, a licensing renewal with only $30.1M of 2027 RPO, and the AI Overviews securities class action. Basis caveat (skeptic point): the 'non-GAAP' peer EPS is not uniform. META, GOOGL, NFLX and SPOT expense SBC (median ~22x), while PINS, SNAP, APP, TTD, DUOL, ROKU and MTCH add it back (median 12.0x). Reddit's SBC is ~12% of revenue, among the highest, so applying the blended 17.6x median to SBC-excluded EPS flatters it. That is why I weight a GAAP-basis method and an SBC-burdened FCF method equally with it.

thesis_break_reason: $108 is ~9% below the 52-week low ($119.27), 19x taxed CY27 GAAP EPS ($5.57), 13.3x taxed CY27 adjusted EPS and ~11.6x ex the ~$13.5/share of net cash. Those are PINS/SNAP-like multiples for a company growing 30%+. Trading there would most likely mean the market is pricing structural traffic loss (a Google referral or licence break, sustained US DAUq declines or a guide-down) rather than ordinary 70%-vol noise. I keep $108 against the supervisor's $105 because my bear case centres at $100 and a break should sit just above it.

reasoning: Supervisor corrections adopted. (1) My round-1 median compared Reddit's GAAP 21.5x with a mostly adjusted peer median. I rebuilt it on one basis (StockAnalysis CY27 consensus, December FYs, SPOT in USD) for 11 peers, with a median of 17.6x. I verified META, SNAP, APP, ROKU and MTCH myself; PINS CY27 is behind SA's paywall, so I used $2.40 (Yahoo, matching the supervisor). (2) ROKU updated to $3.95 (38.7x) and kept as the top of the range. MTCH added. (3) The $7.07 consensus is almost untaxed (full valuation allowance; H1'26 tax ~$5.7M on ~$463M pretax), so I tax everything at 22%. (4) Dropped the 10% EPS haircut to avoid double-counting. Where I differ: the supervisor applies 17.6x to SBC-excluded EPS, but within the peer set only the SBC-expensing mega-caps trade near 22x, while SBC-excluding peers sit at a ~12x median. Reddit's SBC is ~12% of revenue, so I give equal weight to a GAAP-basis P/E ($151) and an SBC-burdened FCF yield ($160) next to the median P/E ($170). The blend is $160, vs the supervisor's $168. I also compute taxed CY27 GAAP EPS at $5.57, not ~$5.9. Skeptic evidence this round: the class action is from June 2025 (class period Oct 2024 - May 2025), still at an early stage and not new. Short interest is ~14% of float. DA Davidson cut its PT to $185 on weak September traffic, and Similarweb shows visits -3.2% m/m (single panel, directional only). I found no new short report, debt or accounting flag; the balance sheet is clean ($2.79B cash, no debt). Scenarios $100/$160/$225 at 25/50/25 give a mean of $161.25, within 1% of the $160 fair value. The ladder is a lognormal mixture (bear sigma 0.40, base/bull 0.30, centred on the scenario prices), median ~$152 with an effective log-sd of ~43%. I fattened the far tails by hand (P>=303 0.045, P>=379 0.015, P>=61 0.955) because the realized vol is 70% and the stock has already moved -55%/+120% within a year. The ladder's median sits at spot and its mean is near fair value: the skeptic case argues against the $210 sell-side median, not for collapse. Research was limited to ~10 queries this round.
